entries.clue: Press often played with by Trump (4)

a golf club; Trump is a keen golfer who owns many courses

annotation.surface: The press as a toy Trump likes to play with.
annotation.walkthrough: "Press" wants to be the newspapers Trump spars with; it is the verb for smoothing clothes, and the second half points to his golf bag.
annotation.definitionFit: As a verb it is a plain synonym of press, smoothing cloth with heat; as a noun it is a golf club, and Trump plays constantly.

annotation.definitionFit: What Conservatives were unhappy with was Badenoch's running of the party, her leadership.

entries.clue: A craving to snap: "Dom is a pain!" (10)

annotation.definitionNote: "a craving" is loose for the uncountable noun, meaning a craving for drink

entries.clue: see 14ac.

entries.clue: Like the politician's reductive announcements of crunch measure? (4-4)

blocks.note: politicians reduce policy to soundbites, short and easily swallowed
a crunch is one chomp, so this is the amount taken in one mouthful

annotation.surface: A jab at politicians who boil a crisis policy down to slogans.
annotation.walkthrough: "Crunch measure" reads as an emergency policy at a crunch point; the question mark flags that it means the amount of one mouthful.
annotation.definitionFit: It means small and easy to take in, as soundbites are, and literally the size of one mouthful.

entries.clue: Guiding principle has Democrat on notice perhaps around Republican (8)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: NOTICE is one possible arrangement of these letters, so perhaps they belong in another
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around R

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
NOTICE rearranged
R is the abbreviation for Republican

annotation.surface: A political principle that puts the Democrats on notice over the Republicans.
annotation.walkthrough: "On notice" is a set phrase in the surface, but "on" only joins D to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a principle or set of beliefs that guides policy.

entries.clue: (& 18dn.) Demonic Bake-off host, at first a staunch right-winger (4)

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the first letter of host

annotation.surface: A sinister presenter of The Great British Bake Off revealed as a hardline conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a TV baking contest, so "Bake-off host" looks like a presenter; the hyphen hides the anagram signal "off". Kemi Badenoch became Conservative leader in 2024.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Kemi Badenoch is a Conservative politician on the right of her party.

entries.clue: Campish habit? (4,5)

annotation.definitionFit: A tent dress is a loose, wide dress that hangs like a tent.

entries.clue: A strict believer in truth as 'idiotic' (5)

annotation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly observant Jewish movement.

entries.clue: Putin's thing: breaking arms limit, crushing independence (10)

indicatorNotes.crushing: the rearranged letters squeeze I inside them

entries.clue: (& 6dn./22dn.) Shroud to go here? Never! (4,2)

the phrase for a flat refusal

annotation.surface: Someone refusing outright a plan to wrap them in a shroud.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: where does a shroud go? Over a corpse, your own.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of saying never, and literally where a shroud is laid.

entries.clue: Ex-president's ire seen to explode on taking question (10)

entries.clue: A PM told off on accepting Cyclops as moderator (8)

annotation.walkthrough: A setter often calls themselves I; here Cyclops names himself, and the one eye of a cyclops suits the letter I.

entries.clue: Nothing gained by "hot and cold" Truss's comeback? (5)

annotation.walkthrough: "Hot and cold" suggests blowing hot and cold, fickleness; it is just the two tap letters.

entries.clue: Is put off by dickhead's rash (6)
